local_articles.title: Gaza documentary to premiere at Venice film festival
local_articles.snippet: ROME: A new documentary called “NAZA” from the same directors as the Oscar-winning Israeli-Palestinian production “No Other Land” will premiere at the Venice Film Festival next month, organizers said on Monday. The film, which will be in competition for the Golden Lion award, is about “the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” according to a synopsis published on the film festival website. The film is directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the four co-directors of “No Other Land,” which tells the story of Palestinian activists trying to protect a cluster of villages in the occupied West Bank from demolition by the Israeli military. NAZA is produced by The Guardian and James Wilson (JW Films) and executive-produced by Jonathan Glazer. local_articles.title: Manchester City star Erling Haaland chops off iconic bun ahead of new season
local_articles.snippet: Erling Haaland unveiled a new hair cut for Manchester City's Premier League opener as the Norway star chopped off his iconic flowing blond locks. Haaland unveiled his fresh close-cropped look on his social media accounts on Sunday, along with the comment: "New season, new trim". The 26-year-old posted another image on X showing the various stages of his haircut, which he captioned "Short hair don't care". And just hours later, Haaland walked onto the Etihad Stadium pitch to warm-up with his new look ahead of City's first game of their top-flight campaign against Bournemouth. During an interview with James Corden on Fox Sports in July, Haaland revealed he had maintained his previous style on the advice of retired Sweden star Zlatan Ibrahimovic, another prolific long-haired Scandinavian striker.
